title: Ninths before the Depression; leaving for Alexandria
summary: Asked if ninths predate the Depression, he says yes, then recounts working in a big band in Alexandria and being tied by a debt.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Yeah, he was good on everything. All these people were professional.
Cato. You know? When Cato played ninths on the piano, was that before the depression?
With who? Before depression. When Cato? Depression. Say, when he started playing ninths, was that before depression? I just remember.
Well, when he started playing ninths,

was it before depression? Well, when you started, was it before depression? When I started, I think it was, yeah. Ask him who he was playing with. Who he was playing with then? I was playing with, let me see him. I was in IT. Yeah, I was in IT when I first started playing. But after I left and went to Alexander, we had 17, 18 men in the band, you know? And after that, we had all those fellas over there in Alexander. Every now and then you get a bunch of good musicians. And they'd stick with the little wives, because in Alexander, everywhere you go, it makes 15 cents, 15 cents. That's all you make over there. Nine of them on the holidays, it makes four or five dollars. Well, them boys would jump where they could. That's 20 cents. Really. And the musicians over there had this blur that they'd bend the law to you, you know? When you say you're going and you're quitting, the law comes and say, well, I heard you go, these John Tunkson. I said, all right then. He said, well, you pay John Tunkson that 150 dollars back with your boy for. I said, what? 150 dollars with your boy? I said, that's true, Cap. I said, John, John, Trump, he sent 150 dollars cash, I don't know when. I said, I've been with him three years. I ain't never seen him have that much money. I said, I don't borrow from nobody. I said, that's all right. He said, your name's on the book. I've been blessed with you, see. And then I started saving my money. I started saving my money when I got to a bad ride. I just kept out I had a girlfriend over there. She helped me go to the train that morning. I went to the train, I said, look at those trains with all the hands late. That's where it is. That's where it is. That's where it's going to keep them part of the gutter. They wouldn't say, they don't make nothing over there, you know.
